findings.title: PR-comment helpers are defined on the integration class but invoked on the workflow class
findings.body: The new _truncate_title, get_environment_info, and get_merged_pr_single_issue_template helpers are added to CommitContextIntegration, but GitHubPRCommentWorkflow and GitlabPRCommentWorkflow call self.get_environment_info() and self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(); those workflows inherit from PRCommentWorkflow/OpenPRCommentWorkflow, not CommitContextIntegration. The helper also calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title even though _truncate_title was defined on CommitContextIntegration. Generating the first suspect-issue comment will therefore raise AttributeError and fail the PR/MR comment workflow instead of posting the comment. The helpers should live on PRCommentWorkflow (or be called via self.integration) and the truncation call should reference the class that actually defines it.

findings.title: Table-widget feature-flag path discards the real table data
findings.body: When the organization has the use-table-widget-visualization feature, tableResultComponent renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded columns=[] and a hardcoded empty tableData ({data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}) instead of converting the current result (result.data, result.meta, fields/eventView, aliases, custom renderers). Every table widget for a flagged organization will render an empty table regardless of the query results. The flagged branch must pass the actual table result data/meta and column definitions, or not be wired into the production chart path yet.

findings.title: Error timestamps and replay-segment timestamps are compared in different units
findings.body: fetch_error_details stores the error event timestamp from nodestore, which is epoch seconds, while replay recording-segment (rrweb) events carry epoch milliseconds. gen_request_data then directly compares error_events[i]['timestamp'] < event.get('timestamp'), so with real data an error timestamp in seconds will almost always be smaller than a segment timestamp in milliseconds and all errors will be emitted before the first breadcrumb (or in the wrong position), destroying the chronological context sent to Seer. Normalize both sides to the same unit (for example multiply the error timestamp by 1000) before sorting/comparing; the added tests mask this by using seconds for the segment timestamps as well.

findings.title: Browser reports with neither age nor timestamp (or with age=0 plus timestamp) pass validation
findings.body: age and timestamp are both declared required=False and there is no object-level validation requiring exactly one of them, so a report missing both fields is accepted and counted. The field validators also test self.initial_data.get('age')/get('timestamp') for truthiness, so a payload with age=0 and a timestamp present bypasses the mutual-exclusion check even though 0 is a legitimate age value. Add a validate() method that requires exactly one of age/timestamp using presence ('in' / is not None) rather than truthiness.

findings.title: Hidden span attributes are only hidden while a search query is active
findings.body: sortedAndFilteredAttributes returns the full sorted attribute list unchanged when the search box is empty, and only applies the HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES exclusion (is_segment, project_id, received) inside the branch that runs when a search query is present. As a result these internal attributes are shown in the default attributes view and then mysteriously disappear as soon as the user starts typing. Apply the hidden-attribute filter unconditionally before/regardless of the search-term filter.

findings.title: Unsuccessful summary generation with feedback present renders an empty summary panel
findings.body: tooFewFeedbacks is only set when numFeedbacksUsed === 0 and success is false. If the summary endpoint returns success=false with summary=null after having used one or more feedbacks (for example an LLM failure), FeedbackSummary does not hide itself (it only hides on tooFewFeedbacks or isError, and this is a successful HTTP response) and renders the 'Feedback Summary' header with an empty body. The hook/component should treat a missing summary or success=false as a hide condition, not only the zero-feedback case.
